questions.prompt: A particle has a \(5\,\mathrm{N}\) force to the right. What single force keeps it in equilibrium?
questions.answer: The balancing force must be equal and opposite: \(5\,\mathrm{N}\) to the left.

questions.prompt: Find the weight of a \(6.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) object near Earth's surface, using \(g=9.8\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}\).
An \(80\,\mathrm{N}\) load is supported by two identical vertical strings. Find the tension in each string.
A force of \(50\,\mathrm{N}\) acts \(30^\circ\) above the positive \(x\)-axis. Find its \(x\)- and \(y\)-components.
A \(100\,\mathrm{N}\) lamp hangs from two identical ropes, each \(30^\circ\) above the horizontal. Find the tension in each rope.
A \(10.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) block rests on a frictionless \(20^\circ\) slope and is held by a rope parallel to the slope. Find the rope tension and normal reaction.
questions.answer:
Along the slope:
\[
T=mg\sin20^\circ=10.0(9.8)\sin20^\circ=33.5\,\mathrm{N}
\]
Perpendicular to the slope:
\[
N=mg\cos20^\circ=92.1\,\mathrm{N}
\]

questions.prompt: A force \(\vec{F}=30\hat{\imath}-40\hat{\jmath}\,\mathrm{N}\) acts on a particle. What single additional force puts the particle in equilibrium?
A \(50\,\mathrm{N}\) weight is held by a cable at \(40^\circ\) above horizontal and a second horizontal cable. Find both cable tensions.
questions.answer:
Vertical balance gives
\[
T\sin40^\circ=50
\]
\[
T=77.8\,\mathrm{N}
\]
Horizontal balance gives
\[
T_h=T\cos40^\circ=59.6\,\mathrm{N}
\]

questions.prompt: A knot has forces \(20\,\mathrm{N}\) east and \(15\,\mathrm{N}\) north acting on it. Find the third force needed for equilibrium, as a magnitude and direction.
questions.answer:
The third force must cancel the resultant:
\[
\vec{F}_3=-20\hat{\imath}-15\hat{\jmath}\,\mathrm{N}
\]
\[
|\vec{F}_3|=\sqrt{20^2+15^2}=25\,\mathrm{N}
\]
Its direction is \(36.9^\circ\) south of west.

questions.prompt: A \(12.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) mass hangs from two ropes. The left rope is \(50^\circ\) above horizontal and the right rope is \(35^\circ\) above horizontal. Find the two tensions and identify which rope is more heavily loaded.
questions.answer:
Let \(T_L\) be the left-rope tension and \(T_R\) the right-rope tension.
\[
T_L\cos50^\circ=T_R\cos35^\circ
\]
\[
T_L\sin50^\circ+T_R\sin35^\circ=12.0(9.8)
\]
Solving gives
\[
T_R=75.9\,\mathrm{N},\qquad T_L=96.7\,\mathrm{N}
\]
So the left rope is more heavily loaded.

questions.prompt: A \(5.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) lamp is held by a horizontal cable to the left and a cable \(35^\circ\) above horizontal to the right. A fan adds a steady \(18\,\mathrm{N}\) force to the right on the lamp. Find both cable tensions.
questions.answer:
Vertical balance:
\[
T_R\sin35^\circ=5.0(9.8)
\]
\[
T_R=85.4\,\mathrm{N}
\]
Horizontal balance (rightward fan force included):
\[
T_L=T_R\cos35^\circ+18
\]
\[
T_L=88.0\,\mathrm{N}
\]

questions.prompt: A load is held by two cables. The left cable is \(30^\circ\) above horizontal and can withstand \(150\,\mathrm{N}\); the right cable is \(50^\circ\) above horizontal and can withstand \(180\,\mathrm{N}\). In addition, a horizontal wind applies \(40\,\mathrm{N}\) to the right on the load. Find the largest load weight and mass that can be held in equilibrium.
questions.answer:
Horizontal balance with rightward wind force \(40\,\mathrm N\):
\[
T_R\cos50^\circ+40=T_L\cos30^\circ
\]
So
\[
T_R=\frac{\cos30^\circ}{\cos50^\circ}T_L-\frac{40}{\cos50^\circ}
\]
The right cable reaches its limit first (set \(T_R=180\,\mathrm N\)):
\[
T_L=179.5\,\mathrm{N}
\]
But this exceeds the left-cable limit \(150\,\mathrm N\), so left cable is actually limiting.
Set \(T_L=150\,\mathrm N\):
\[
T_R=1.347(150)-\frac{40}{\cos50^\circ}=140.3\,\mathrm N
\]
The supported weight is
\[
W=T_L\sin30^\circ+T_R\sin50^\circ=182.5\,\mathrm{N}
\]
\[
m=\frac{W}{g}=\frac{182.5}{9.8}=18.6\,\mathrm{kg}
\]
